item.title: American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, described the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that neither the Nigerian government nor anyone else in the country paid her the reported sum. She said her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to see the country for herself. “I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself. “This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote. The denial comes amid controversy surrounding her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday, and reports alleging that she was linked to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to clarify whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying contract and disclose the details of the arrangement. In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but maintained that the Presidency should clarify whether the interview formed part of the contract. Atiku demanded the publication of the contract, details of the payment and the release of the full, unedited recording of the interview. He also questioned the nature of the engagement, arguing that the Presidency should establish whether the encounter was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. The former vice president further asked the government to disclose who authorised the payment, the source of the funds and whether public money was involved. The controversy followed London’s earlier social media posts praising the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump. In one of the posts, she described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, saying the security cooperation between both countries was producing results and could create further economic and trade opportunities. She also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria in efforts to strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. However, the posts were subsequently deleted, while London restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian

item.title: NASA Sets Coverage for Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Launch, Prelaunch
item.description: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 mission launched Saturday, April 11, 2026, aboard the company’s Cygnus XL spacecraft atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: Northrop Grumman NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 10:47 a.m. EST, Sunday, Nov. 29, for the next launch delivering science investigations, supplies, and equipment to the International Space Station. The agency also will hold a prelaunch media teleconference on Monday, Nov. 23. Filled with approximately 11,000 pounds of cargo, the Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The mission is known as NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25. After arriving at the International Space Station, NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, who are living and working aboard the space station, will use the Canadarm2 robotic arm to capture the Cygnus XL on Tuesday, Dec. 1. Ground controllers then will install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Highlights of space station research and technology demonstrations being delivered aboard this Cygnus XL spacecraft include experiments to improve drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis, predict cancer spread, and advance treatments for muscle loss, as well as improve radiation sensing and advance food production for future long-duration missions. The spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the orbiting laboratory until May 2027, then depart with several thousand pounds of disposal items and other unneeded cargo, burning up harmlessly during re-entry. Northrop Grumman named the spacecraft the S.S. James “Jim” A. Lovell in honor of the former NASA astronaut. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Monday, Nov. 23 12 p.m.: Prelaunch teleconference will stream on NASA’s YouTube channel with the following participants: Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program Jennifer Buchli, chief scientist, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program Dave Schiller, vice president, civil space and sciences, Northrop Grumman Jared Metter, director, flight reliability, SpaceX To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 11 a.m., Nov. 23, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. The agency’s media credenti

item.title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
item.description: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2026 Globe Soccer Awards: Messi, Ronaldo, Dembele, Yamal included [Full List]
item.description: Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Lamine Yamal are among the high-profile footballers nominated for the 2026 Beyond Developments Globe Soccer Awards. The nominees for the 17th edition of the awards were unveiled on Wednesday through the organisers’ official website, with Paris Saint-Germain and Spain among the prominent names following their successes in the UEFA Champions League and 2026 FIFA World Cup. Dembele, who won the Best Men’s Player award last year, has been shortlisted again alongside 25 other players for the individual prize. Meanwhile, Ronaldo will be seeking to retain the Best Middle East Player award after making the 2026 shortlist. The awards ceremony is billed for December 28 in the United Arab Emirates, while public voting across 12 categories commenced on Wednesday and will end on November 30. The organisers disclosed that fans would determine the first round of voting, with their votes combined with those of the Globe Soccer Jury during the second round. The jury features several prominent former football figures, including Marcello Lippi, Antonio Conte, Iker Casillas and Luis Figo. The previous edition attracted more than 30 million votes from over 200 countries and territories. According to the organisers, supporters can cast their votes through the official website, vote.globesoccer.com, or the Globe Soccer mobile application. item.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
item.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart. "I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar said. In the new study, the scientists estimated that the eruption expelled an amount of material equal to about 0.1 to 0.2 times the mass of the sun . "Stars engulfing their companions have been theorized for many decades, and this event provides the first observations of this theoretical prediction," Karambelkar said. Although these findings suggest that two stars — a binary system nicknamed "Bao" — merged into one, "it is not the only possibility," Karambelkar said. item.title: 2027: SDP pledges free education, vows to tackle insecurity
item.description: …Promises N200 petrol, affordable housing, jobs By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has pledged to tackle poverty, insecurity, unemployment and other socio-economic challenges facing Nigerians if elected into power in the 2027 general elections. The party said addressing poverty and economic hardship was critical to tackling insecurity, insurgency, kidnapping and other criminal activities across the country. Speaking on Wednesday at the SDP presidential campaign rally in Yola, Adamawa State, the party’s National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, urged Nigerians to make informed political choices ahead of the 2027 elections, saying poverty and insecurity required purposeful leadership and people-oriented policies. Gombe urged residents to support the party’s presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and his running mate, Professor Usman Bugaje, saying the ticket was committed to addressing the country’s challenges through policies that would create economic opportunities, improve living conditions and restore public confidence in governance. In a statement issued on Wednesday by the National Coordinator of the SDP Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Yunusa Tanko, the party chairman urged Adamawa residents to assess the records, character and policy proposals of candidates before deciding whom to support in the 2027 elections. In his remarks, the presidential candidate, Adebayo, said an SDP-led administration would redefine governance by ensuring that public resources were deployed for the benefit of Nigerians, with priority given to security, education, healthcare, housing, food security and employment. Describing the SDP as a party founded on democratic values and social justice, he said its philosophy was anchored on the belief that political power belonged to the people and that government resources must be used to improve their welfare. He said his proposed administration would focus on implementing the fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy contained in Chapter Two of the Constitution, particularly provisions relating to poverty reduction and citizens’ welfare. “Government is the organisation selected by you through your votes. Government must provide security, accountability, good food, affordable housing, quality education and accessible healthcare. It must work for the people who elected it,” he said. On security, Adebayo identified terrorism, banditry and kidnapping as some of Nigeria’s most pressing challenges, promising decisive measures to address them through improved security management and better support for security personnel. He also pledged to strengthen the welfare and operational capacity of the armed forces and other security agencies, saying personnel responsible for protecting the country would receive the necessary equipment, funding and support to discharge their duties. item.title: ADC leaders lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, National Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkareem, Wednesday, said some leaders of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, as lazy and entitled politicians. Abdulkareem also said they had failed to establish clear terms for the coalition they were seeking to build. He faulted the ADC leaders for failing to agree on power-sharing arrangements and a presidential candidate before bringing politicians into the coalition, saying the North should not continue to dominate the country’s leadership. Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he said: “I used to term some of the people I see in ADC as lazy politicians. Right from time, even when they are constructing this coalition that they talk about, instead of them finding a way of doing what the All Progressives Congress, APC, had done, put everything in black and white that we want to come for a coalition. And this coalition, this is the person that we want to be the president, or we are zoning this part of what we are going to do to this part of the country. “At that time, everybody that is coming into that coalition knows exactly why he’s coming, so it’s not going to be any problem in trying to see who becomes what. Immediately we started this thing they started to say Peter Obi is a vice-presidential candidate to Atiku. What kind of coalition is that? The entitlement from the elite, I find it very annoying sometimes. “You just decide the North. Which North? You talk like you own something that you. There is no right given to Atiku, for example, to say everybody must surrender. We have been ruling from Gen Ibrahim Babangida (retd) to the late Muhammadu Buhari. But look at where we are. “Go and see our streets. Go and see our villages. Look at how we have been ravaged. But since somebody is still coming today, trying to play this northern card at this level, it’s time to start thinking how can we hire somebody, irrespective of where he’s coming from, irrespective of religion or tribe, somebody that we know he has this integrity, somebody that can make these public funds to be used for public good, somebody that can be accountable, not people that are old and full of entitlement.” The post ADC leaders lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lagos-Ibadan Expressway gridlock leaves commuters stranded for hours
item.description: Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on Wednesday following the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which triggered a massive traffic gridlock. The congestion paralysed movement on both sides of the expressway, with motorists travelling towards Lagos held up from the Redemption Camp area to Aseese bus stop, while those heading towards Ogun State were trapped from the Long Bridge area to Aseese. The scale of the gridlock left commuters spending unusually long hours on journeys that would ordinarily take a fraction of the time. One of our correspondents, who boarded a commercial vehicle from Ibadan shortly after 11am, did not arrive in Magboro, Ogun State, until about 5.30pm. Another motorist lamented spending eight hours travelling from Mowe to Magboro, highlighting the severity of the traffic situation. The gridlock persisted as late as 10pm, with both sections of the expressway reportedly almost completely blocked. Efforts by some motorists to escape the congestion by driving against the flow of traffic further compounded the situation, as they obstructed vehicles moving in the appropriate lanes. With vehicular movement severely restricted, commercial motorcyclists cashed in on the situation, making brisk business by conveying stranded commuters through alternative routes. The renewed construction work on the pedestrian bridge at Aseese was identified as the immediate trigger of the traffic disruption. The post Lagos-Ibadan Expressway gridlock leaves commuters stranded for hours appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FIFA picks Amokachi, four others to oversee NFF until May 2027
item.description: World football governing body FIFA has appointed former Super Eagles striker Daniel Amokachi and four others to a five-member normalisation committee tasked with overseeing the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF). The committee will be chaired by former NFF electoral committee chairman Sampson Ebomhe and is expected to manage the federation’s transition and organise fresh elections for a new leadership. Its mandate will run until May 31, 2027, at the latest. FIFA communicated the appointments in a letter sent to the NFF secretariat on Wednesday, following consultations with the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Other members of the committee are governance expert Dr Joe Abah, veteran sports journalist and administrator Godwin Enakhena, and Amina Yerima. “We refer to the decision of the Bureau of the FIFA Council of 22 October 2026 to appoint a normalisation committee for the Nigeria Football Federation. “In this respect, following consultation with CAF, we hereby communicate the composition of the normalisation committee as follows: Mr Sampson Ebomhe (chairman), Dr Joe Abah (member), Mr Godwin Enakhena (member), Ms Amina Yerima (member) and Mr Daniel Amokachi (member),” the letter read. The world football governing body said the appointees would commence their duties immediately, subject to eligibility screening by its Review Committee in line with FIFA Governance Regulations. Their final confirmation will depend on the outcome of the screening exercise. FIFA also prohibited members of the committee from contesting any position in the forthcoming NFF elections, regardless of whether they resign or have their appointments revoked. “None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances, including in the event that their mandate as a member of the normalisation committee is revoked or that they resign from their position,” the letter added. FIFA further stated that it could, in consultation with CAF, withdraw the appointment of any committee member or expand the committee by appointing additional members. The intervention follows the resignation of NFF President Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive committee on August 27, 2026, amid growing criticism of the country’s football administration. The development disrupted arrangements for the NFF elective congress scheduled for September 27, prompting FIFA and CAF to step in and approve the establishment of a normalisation committee to supervise the transition. Ebomhe, who will lead the committee, has previously held several positions in Nigerian sports administration. In August 2025, he was appointed vice-chairman of the seven-member electoral committee established by the National Sports Commission to conduct elections into national sports federations. item.title: Anthropic decides to go head-to-head with GTA VI release, schedules IPO for the same day
item.description: Well, it’s official: Anthropic will become the first publicly-traded frontier AI lab in history come the opening of markets on Thursday. The company kicked off its IPO roadshow last week, announcing plans to offer 825 million shares with an IPO price between $70 and $78 a share when sales begin Thursday. The company's most recent SEC filing cites that price range but allows for the possibility of a higher price, which should be determined Wednesday night. Late on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported that Anthropic would price at $83, citing people familiar. Whatever the case, Anthropic is likely to be valued at more than $1 trillion. Anthropic’s debutante ball has been on the horizon for a while, and documents leaked in late September made it all the more inevitable as the company’s finances revved up and it sought to capture the momentum of its best quarter to date before things start to tail off. The company revised its IPO documents on November 2, warning that the 12x growth it was touting was unlikely to continue in the long term due to compute infrastructure investments to the tune of nearly $900 billion it was on the hook for over the next few years. "In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our revenue was $33.2 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%," the revised prospectus reads. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all." It’s possible, in other words, that Anthropic may never be a money maker despite the hype and its position as the first mover. The IPO prospectus is short on answers to critical questions and leaves a lot unanswered - like, for example, whether it’s going to actually be able to pay its bills. "Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the updated prospectus admits. Investors don’t seem to care right now, though. Anthropic already has compute commitments amounting to roughly $70.7 billion in the next 12 months. That’s just shy of its $81 billion run-rate as of October 31. Expect more hot air to be injected tomorrow, adding additional surface tension and the possibility of even more losses if, and when, this monster pops. ®

item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Can’t Alter State Police Bill, He’ll Definitely Sign It — Omole
item.description: Lawyer and author Charles Omole has said that he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to make an alteration to the National Policing Bill transmitted to him by the National Assembly. Omole, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday. He explained that altering the bill would return the process to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for their approval. Omole noted further that the constitutional amendment is not the meat and bone of policing but simply allows state police to exist, while the National Policing Bill specifies the structure and functions of the state police. He, however, said that the National Policing Bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had gone through. He explained that while the 36 states would have their own police service, the police in the Federal Capital Territory would be under the control of the federal police service. item.title: AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites
item.description: Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX. These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services. “At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register . “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.” As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years. Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently. Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.” “We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.” NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million ), and F5 maintains the open source version. On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible. CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 , both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5. “Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy.” Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concep t to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8. Xint found three other NGINX flaws, plus a sepa

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
item.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind , as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come." MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent , with NASA losing communication with the orbiter. An investigation later found that the probe sent its final signal on Dec. 6, 2025 as it was heading behind Mars (as seen from Earth). item.title: Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state. Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , said the governor had not scored more than 20 per cent in performance. The PDP candidate said that leadership should be about performance and about the people. “In fact, I can tell you on a scale of one to 100, you can give him like 15 to 20 per cent in performance,” he said. “He still remains someone that I respect, but of course that, completely, is different from politics.” ﻿ He alleged that the governor defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) when he could not cope with the crisis in the PDP. He, however, said that the governor did not leave with up to 15 per cent of the members of the PDP, insisting that Plateau is a PDP state. “You know, a man’s strength and leadership qualities are being tested when there are crises, but the governor couldn’t stand the crisis. He left for APC, and so there was an opening in the PDP to contest for governorship because, of course, the truth is this. Plateau has been a PDP state. “You can’t take that away from Plateau State, right? And so there was a vacancy, and so somebody needed to fill in the gap. And so even with the crisis, we believed in the PDP,” the candidate said. “Mutfwang did not live with 15, 20 per cent of people, I mean, in PDP to APC. The people, in fact, not even 10 per cent, because the people that followed him to APC are his appointees, and that’s the truth. “Ninety per cent of people on the Plateau still believe in the PDP.” Ropshik said that Plateau is one of the frontrunners in the Rainbow Coalition. He also said that he was working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. Asked whether he was not confusing his followers by telling them to vote for the APC in the January 16 presidential election, and the PDP in the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state, Ropshik said, “No, no, no, I am not reading because now if we want to be sincere to ourselves, the PDP presidential candidate, we all know that there’s no chance for him to win the election. “And so why should we now waste the votes? We must find a platform to identify; what we’re after is good governance.” The post Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
item.description: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core . Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency's (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: "The s ecure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened. " The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance. Read full article Comments

item.title: Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger reach deal on military pursuit of terrorists
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Nigeria and three neighbouring countries — Cameroon, Chad and Niger — have reportedly agreed to allow military forces to pursue terrorists, armed bandits and other criminal groups up to five kilometres across their shared borders. The arrangement is aimed at strengthening regional counterterrorism operations and preventing fleeing militants from escaping military pressure by crossing into neighbouring territories. The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed the agreement in Abuja, explaining that it would enable security forces to sustain hot pursuit of fleeing terrorists across border areas. The agreement is expected to strengthen military cooperation among the four countries, particularly in tackling transnational security threats posed by Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and other armed criminal groups operating around the Lake Chad Basin and adjoining border communities. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was receiving real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training support from the United States to enhance its counterterrorism capabilities and improve the effectiveness of military operations. The Defence Minister said Nigerian troops had recently neutralised several terrorist and bandit commanders during overnight operations across the North-East and North-West regions. He said the cross-border pursuit arrangement is particularly significant for communities along Nigeria’s borders with Cameroon, Chad and Niger, where terrorist groups have exploited porous boundaries to evade security operations and sustain their activities. In Cameroon’s Far North Region, Boko Haram and ISWAP activities have continued to pose security challenges, making closer military coordination between neighbouring countries critical to addressing the threat. Details of the agreement, including its operational procedures, rules of engagement and safeguards for civilians in affected border communities, have not been provided in the information released. The arrangement signals a renewed push for regional military cooperation, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations against terrorist networks whose activities extend beyond national boundaries. The post Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger reach deal on military pursuit of terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gun can kill terrorists, only education can kill terrorism – Buratai
item.description: The former Chief of Army Staff, retired Lt.-Gen. Tukur Buratai has called for inclusive education and wider access to learning opportunities, saying they are critical to addressing the conditions that sustain terrorism and violent extremism in Nigeria. Buratai made the call at the 2026 Young Adult Literature Prize Award and unveiling of the 2025 anthology of the T.Y. Buratai Literary Initiative (TYBLI), on Wednesday in Nasarawa State. The former Nigerian Ambassador to Benin Republic said military force alone could not defeat terrorism without deliberate investment in education, intellectual development and the minds of young Nigerians. “Gun can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism,” he declared. Buratai said national development must go beyond infrastructure, military strength and economic resources to include the intellectual capacity, creative imagination and moral consciousness of citizens. He stressed that young Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds, needed equal opportunities, platforms and encouragement to develop their talents and contribute meaningfully to society. The former COAS said the initiative was established on the conviction that great nations were built not only by strong armies and economies but also by ideas, literature and educated citizens. He urged universities to promote young adult literature through research, teaching and programmes that encouraged creativity, critical thinking and intellectual development. “A school that produces excellent academic results but neglects imagination and critical thinking has not fully prepared its students for the future,” he said. Buratai said the initiative had, since 2023, provided a platform for young Nigerians from diverse backgrounds to demonstrate their creativity and move from passive consumption to active production of literature. He described the unveiling of the 2025 anthology as another milestone, providing a permanent record of the imagination, creativity and achievements of young authors. He also announced plans to introduce full scholarships for deserving winners within the next three to five years, to enable them to complete their education. In a goodwill message, the Vice-Chancellor of Nasarawa State University, Keffi, Prof. Sa’adatu Liman, described young adult literature as an important bridge between childhood and adulthood. Liman said literature helped young people confront questions of identity, courage, faith, justice and leadership through stories that reflected their experiences. She described the initiative as an investment in human development and nation-building, pledging the university’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with TYBLI. Also, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Prof. Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, commended the initiative for recognising the importance of academic leadership, scholarship and research mentorship. item.title: FAAC shares N2.4trn among FG, states, LGs for October
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government. The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday. The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion. According to the communiqué sent to media houses by Bawa Mokwa, Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Wednesday night, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion. Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion. The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion. The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion. In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased. The post FAAC shares N2.4trn among FG, states, LGs for October appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu hails Alake of Egbaland’s 21-year reign
item.description: ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎President Bola Tinubu has paid tribute to the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo III, describing his 21 years on the throne as a testament to selfless service and dedication to his people’s welfare. ‎ ‎The President in a tribute marking the monarch’s anniversary, praised his commitment to development, cultural preservation and responsible leadership. ‎ ‎“Your Majesty, 21 years on the throne is no ordinary milestone. It is a remarkable testament to your selfless service and dedication to your people’s welfare,” the President said. ‎ ‎Tinubu saluted the monarch’s military career before his ascension, highlighting the principles that defined his service to the nation. ‎ ‎“Your Majesty, your journey to the revered throne was preceded by your distinguished and illustrious military career, where discipline, courage, patriotism, loyalty, and a deep sense of duty formed the core of your guiding principles in serving the nation.” ‎ ‎The President said the Alake’s reign had witnessed development within the Egba kingdom and across the state, underscoring the contribution of traditional institutions to governance and development. ‎ ‎“For 21 remarkable years, your reign has witnessed tremendous development, not only within the Egba kingdom but also across the state. ‎ ‎”These strides in development stand as enduring reminders of the invaluable role of the traditional institution in complementing governments of the day for overall development.” ‎ ‎Tinubu also commended the monarch’s dedication to preserving cultural heritage and acknowledged the influence of his counsel on elected leaders. ‎ ‎“Your unwavering commitment to preserving and promoting our rich cultural heritage deserves commendation and emulation across all strata,” he said. ‎ ‎“Your words of advice, with consistent emphasis on responsible leadership, humility, accountability, service to the people, and respect for institutions, continue to guide us as elected leaders of the people.” ‎ ‎Congratulating the sons and daughters of Egbaland, the President said God had answered their prayers for a king distinguished by wisdom, humility and dedication to service. ‎ ‎“As you celebrate this remarkable anniversary, I congratulate the sons and daughters of Egbaland that Almighty God answered their prayers for a King filled with wisdom, dedication to service, humility and whose reign will be known for peace and development.” ‎ ‎The President concluded his tribute with prayer, saying: “May Almighty God grant Your Majesty sound health, renewed strength, divine wisdom and many more fruitful and item.title: To rank the world's biggest supercomputers, we're gonna need a bigger bench
item.description: For decades, the Top500 list has tirelessly ranked the world’s biggest, most powerful, and often most unique publicly-known supercomputers. With the rise of generative AI, the list no longer lives up to its name. China’s Lineshine supercomputer at 2.2 exaFLOPS of double precision compute in the High-Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark may be the top system on the bi-annual ranking, but it’s nowhere near the biggest compute cluster in the world. Superclusters like SpaceXAI’s Colossus, Meta’s Promethius, and OpenAI’s Stargate pack hundreds of thousands of GPUs, dwarfing anything on the Top500 today. “These [companies] are not interested in submitting to the Top500,” Eth Zürich’s Torsten Hoefler said during his Supercomputing address this week. It’s a dilemma that the founders of the Top500 ranking are now grappling with. And some believe it may be time for a rethink. “What’s really needed for tracking that more appropriately is not just a different benchmark but also different methodology,” Top500 author Erich Strohmaier said. For a long time, Strohmaier explains, compute capability was roughly aligned with capacity. What happened in the last few years with AI is “capacity really pulled ahead of capability in terms of market size,” he said. “We were and we still are very focused on capability.” By capability, Strohmaier is referring to the ability to run one code across the entire cluster. “Our prime rule for benchmarking is, you have to benchmark your whole system with one code and you cannot just add two parts up to make up a number,” he explained. This is problematic for the large clusters major hyperscalers and cloud providers are now building to fuel the AI boom. “All those systems are capacity systems,” Strohmaier said. They’re not designed to run one piece of code but have instead been architected to run many, many smaller or medium-sized code instantiations, which may include training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and of course inference. Because of this, Strohmaier says, it wouldn’t be reasonable to expect SpaceXAI to run something High-Performance Linpack (HPL) on a cluster like Colossus. But these clusters are still worth tracking. They'll just need a new benchmark better suited to judging the capability of these arrays while at the same time preventing operators from gaming the system. What shape or form such a benchmark might take remains to be seen. Developing a new benchmark or methodology is no small task, and changing the existing benchmarks isn’t ideal. ”If we do anything to the benchmark itself, we’re going to lose the historic trends, which is extremely valuable,” Hoefler said. Allowing for lower precisions — HPL-MxP already does this to some extent — is one avenue for addressing the fact that these accelerators are increasingly trading FP64 performance for lower-accuracy floating-point data types like FP8 or FP4. Another avenue is developing a separate AI benchmark. This would be immediately applicable to these clusters

item.title: Air strikes kill 21 ISWAP terrorists in Borno
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi In a significant operational success, precision air strikes conducted by the Air Assets of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), between 16 and 17 November 2026, have neutralised 21 Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and severely injured 10 others in separate operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State. A statement signed by Captain Mohammed Goni, Acting Military Information Officer, said, “The first operation followed intelligence reports of ISWAP fighters advancing towards Monguno. “Acting on the intelligence, an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) established surveillance over the area and identified terrorists moving along a bush path northeast of Monguno. “The subsequent precision strike neutralised seven fighters, including members of the terrorist group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network. Further confirmation revealed that Abba Bomma, identified as a key IED team expert, was incapacitated, while four other fighters sustained severe injuries. “In a separate operation at Arinna in the South Lake Chad area, precision air strikes dealt a significant blow to ISWAP’s leadership and operational structure. Among those neutralised was Malkam Sharki, a prominent member of the group’s Shura Council and Amirul Amniya (Provost Commander). “Also neutralised was ABU SAAD, the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu. Twelve additional fighters were eliminated, while five others sustained severe injuries. Several terrorist motorcycles were also destroyed during the operation. “Altogether, the two operations accounted for 21 ISWAP fighters neutralised and 10 severely injured. “The strikes have significantly degraded the group’s leadership structure, disrupted its IED network and weakened its operational capabilities. “The Theatre Command reaffirms its resolve to maintain sustained operational pressure on terrorists until lasting peace and normalcy are restored across the North East. “Residents are encouraged to continue supporting security agencies with credible and timely information.” The post Air strikes kill 21 ISWAP terrorists in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
item.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. (Image credit: William Dummitt via Getty Images) What erased the geological record? In a new study published in the journal Nature, Dhungana and study co-author Nicolas Flament investigated whether activity far below Earth's surface was to blame. Using computer models, they explored how the slow circulation of hot rock within Earth's mantle may have affected the continents over hundreds of millions of years. The results suggest that three major ancient continental regions (Laurentia (modern North America), Baltica (northern Europe) and North China were gradually pushed up during the Neoproterozoic Era, approximately one billion to 540 million years ago. This would have left vast areas of land exposed to weathering and erosion for long periods, allowing water, wind and other processes to wear away rock that had formed much earlier. But removing the rock is only part of the puzzle. They also needed to explain why the gaps

item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Wednesday arraigned a socialite, Halimat Adenike Tejuosho, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Gwagwalada Division, for an alleged N603,400,000.00 job scam. She was arraigned before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering on advance fee fraud, obtaining by false pretence and criminal conduct, according to a statement posted on EFCC’s X page. Count one reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho and Gidado Ibrahim between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court obtained the sum of N603,400,000.00 (Six hundred and three million four hundred thousand naira) from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye under the false pretence that you will facilitate her appointment as the Group Managing Director, GMD of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), which pretence you knew to be false and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 1(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006 and punishable under Section 1(3) of the same Act. Count two reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N259,900,000 (Two Hundred and Fifty-Nine Million, Nine Hundred Thousand Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act. Count four states: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho on 30th September 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N50,000,000 (Fifty Million Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069 and name HALEEMS INTEGRATED SERVICES LIMITED, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act.” Tejuosho pleaded not guilty to all the charges. Following the plea, defence counsel, Chuks Ugwuru, urged the court to grant the defendant bail on liberal terms, noting that all five counts are bailable offences. He said the application was anchored mainly on her ill health, citing a medical report which, he argued, showed that she was critically ill. “The ill health of an accused person is a consideration worthy enough to be reckoned as a ground of special circumstances,” he said, urging Justice Adepoju to exercise his discretion in the defendant’s favour. Responding, lead prosecution counsel, Yahaya Tarfa, said the EFCC opposed the application and had filed a 12-paragraph counter-affidavit with one exhibit, along with a written address. item.title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
item.description: By Chioma Obinna Health experts on Wednesday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos, tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate. She said access to affordable medicines and wider coverage of the National Health Insurance Scheme was equally important in preventing and managing cardiov

item.title: How residents killed BEDC staff for disconnecting building over N300k electricity bill
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE management of the BEDC Electricity Plc on Wednesday called on the security agencies and government to ensure that its 38 years old staff identified as Oscar Nduka Eze who was brutally killed while on duty on Monday gets justice. Eze was reportedly stabbed to death around Idumobi Umunede in the Agbor Unit, Delta State after he disconnected a building said to be owing about N300,000 electricity bill. Shortly after he disconnected the building, he was said to have been trailed to a nearby house by some people suspected to have been from previous place he had gone to work when they reportedly pounced on him and stabbed him severally till he died. Addressing journalists at the company’s office, Acting Managing Director of the company, Jonathan Lawani said the killers wanted to conceal their act but unknown to them, the building which they took him to had security camera. He said “Eze went to work on Monday 16th November 2026 for his official duty to earn a legitimate living. However, at about 12 noon of that same day while he was carrying out his official work along the Idumobi by Umunede within the Agbor Business Unit of our operations in Delta State, some hoodlums, some men who claim to be more powerful than God, who has the power to take life, traced him to a house within the same community and they stabbed him with knife until he died on the spot. Caught on CCTV “What they planned did not work. These people had planned to kill him without any evidence. And what they did was to push him into a compound, a very isolated place where he went to carry out another assignment. Unfortunately for them, that house has a CCTV camera and they were all captured directly. “The simple reason for this is that this officer had disconnected their house for non-payment. The only instrument that have been approved by NERC, the Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission to ask for payment or to demand payment for those who refuse to pay us for our monthly electricity. I want to put it straight that what the late Oscar did was an approved and official assignment. “The house in question owes us almost three hundred thousand naira and he disconnected them for non-payment and left the place quietly.” Lawani said Eze just got married four months ago after his wife died. He said five persons have been arrested in connection to the incident. “We cannot bring him back but we must ensure that justice is served. We will do everything in line with the law to see that justice is served,” he added. Vanguard News The post How residents killed BEDC staff for disconnecting building over N300k electricity bill appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PDP delegation visits injured APC leaders at Gombe hospital
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe In a significant demonstration of political tolerance, sportsmanship and solidarity, the Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has paid a solidarity visit to leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who sustained injuries in a road accident while returning from a campaign rally on Tuesday. The PDP delegation, led by the Director-General of its Campaign Council, Hon. Dan’azumi Adamu Pindiga, visited the injured APC leaders at the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Gombe, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, to express sympathy and wish them a speedy recovery. Those involved in the accident included the APC State Campaign Council Director-General, Hon. Sa’adu Hassan, and the Gombe State APC Chairman, Hon. Dantata Ndus, alongside other party members. Members of the PDP delegation included the party’s State Secretary, Hon. Adamu Abubakar; Hon. Abubakar Walama; Hon. Sani Hassan Dogarai; Hon. Hassan Santana; Hon. Abubakar Bello (Cikasoron Gombe); and Hon. Jalo Ahmed Ganga. During the visit, Pindiga conveyed messages of solidarity and goodwill on behalf of the PDP leader in Gombe State, former Governor, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, OON, PhD, Talban Gombe; the party’s governorship candidate, Professor Isa Ali Pantami; and the entire PDP family in the state. The delegation also offered prayers to Almighty Allah to grant the injured party chieftains and other victims of the accident complete healing, renewed strength and a speedy recovery. Speaking during the visit, the PDP representatives stressed that political differences should not undermine the bonds of brotherhood, humanity and mutual respect among the people of Gombe State. They maintained that, “beyond party affiliations and electoral interests, political actors remain members of one community with shared responsibilities and a common obligation to promote peaceful coexistence”. According to the delegation, “an unfortunate incident involving members of another political party should attract the concern and sympathy of all, irrespective of political leanings”. The visit, coming amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscores the need for political maturity, tolerance and civility among competing parties and their supporters. It also sends a strong message that political competition should be anchored on issues, policies and the contest for public support, rather than hostility, animosity or division. The PDP delegation reiterated its goodwill towards the injured APC leaders and prayed for their full recovery, stressing that humanity must always take precedence over partisan considerations. According to them, “Politics Should Never Come Before Humanity; We Are All Brothers and sisters”. The post PDP delegation visits injured APC leaders at Gombe hospital appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said . Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11. Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together. How the scheme worked From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information. The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over. The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims. The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme. From Scotland to a California courtroom Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said . Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim. Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples. Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed , that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since. What Scattered Spider is Reuters has described Scattered Spider as a loose-knit community of hackers suspected of breaking into dozens of U.S. companies. item.title: Sony’s impressive Bravia 8 II OLED hits a new low price ahead of Black Friday
item.description: The Bravia 8 II has deep and inky blacks, giving great depth to space images. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Black Friday is a great time to save on a new OLED television for your winter movie nights. Though, it turns out that you can already get a great deal on the 65-inch Sony Bravia 8 II , one of our favorite OLED televisions. It’s currently discounted by $1,100 at various retailers, including Amazon , Best Buy , and directly from Sony . That discount brings the price under $2,200, the lowest we’ve seen. You can also save $800 on the 55-inch model, which is typically $2,599.99 ( Amazon , Best Buy , Sony ), but now costs just under $1,800. item.title: US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash
item.description: An American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian users over her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London interviewed Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday and was subsequently photographed with the President and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila. Following the interview, she published several posts on X expressing support for the Nigerian government’s security cooperation with the United States. In one of the posts, London described the US-Nigeria security partnership as one that was “delivering results”, crediting Tinubu and US President Donald Trump for their commitment to tackling terrorism. “The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote. She also described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, expressing optimism that the relationship could create additional economic and trade opportunities for both countries. In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria, particularly on initiatives relating to the protection of religious groups and strengthening relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. However, the posts were subsequently deleted from her X account amid criticism from Nigerian social media users over her engagement with the Tinubu administration. The controversy followed a report by Peoples Gazette alleging that London received $4.5 million for the interview assignment. The allegation generated reactions on social media, with some users questioning the reported payment and the nature of the engagement. Checks on her X account on Wednesday showed that access to the comment section had been restricted, with a notice indicating that only selected accounts could respond to her posts. Before the restriction, some users had questioned her decision to delete the posts praising the Nigerian government’s security partnership with the United States. London had not publicly explained the deletion of the posts or the restriction of comments as of the time of filing this report. The post US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2026 harvest reduces food prices, says Kyari
item.description: …Niger leads rice, yam production — NAERLS report By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has said increased food production during the 2026 wet season has contributed to a reduction in food prices despite persistent challenges in the agricultural sector. Kyari spoke on Wednesday during the presentation of the 2026 Agricultural Performance Survey Report by the Executive Director of the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services (NAERLS), Professor Yusuf Sani, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. The minister said the report indicated an increase in agricultural output compared with 2025, attributing the development to government interventions aimed at boosting food production and improving affordability. He cited reductions in the prices of commodities such as garri and millet, saying the trend reflected improvements in food supply. “When you do comparison between 2025 and 2026, I am not even comparing 2023 and 2026, just within the one year, we have seen prices dropping — garri, millet, and so on and so forth, that has come down,” he said. Kyari added that another harvest was expected within the next month, which he said could further improve food availability. On agricultural mechanisation, he said deliveries under the second phase of the programme were expected within the next two to three months. He also disclosed that the Federal Government planned to release food commodities stored under the Guaranteed Minimum Price (GMP) programme through the Bank of Agriculture to help stabilise market prices. “That is also in the works, and very soon we will announce how the methodology of that release will be made,” he said. On fertiliser supply, Kyari said the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative planned to release three million bags of fertiliser within one month to reduce input costs for farmers. He said the programme, announced by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, was part of efforts to improve agricultural productivity and balance the interests of farmers, processors and consumers. The minister also pointed to increased private-sector investment in agricultural processing, particularly in cocoa, sesame, soybean and shea nut. He said investments by multinational companies in the country’s agricultural sector indicated growing confidence in Nigeria’s business environment. Kyari further disclosed that $33 million had been invested in the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ) programme. He said government interventions over the past three years had contributed to increased productivity across several crop categories, although some crops continued to record declines. Presenting the survey findings, NAERLS Executive Director, Professor Yusuf Sani, said Niger State emerged as the country’s leading producer of rice and yam. He said Ogun State ranked second in rice production, although its rice yield per hectare was lower than that of Niger State. Sani attributed Niger Stat

item.title: Naira weakens to N1,470/$ at parallel market
item.description: The naira depreciated to N1,470 per dollar at the parallel foreign exchange market on Wednesday, its weakest performance since January 28. The latest rate represented a N25, or 1.73 per cent, decline from the N1,445 per dollar quoted on Tuesday. Currency traders, popularly known as Bureau De Change operators, in Lagos quoted the buying rate at N1,450 per dollar and the selling rate at N1,470. The local currency had traded at N1,430 per dollar on Monday, compared with N1,390 on November 13, representing a depreciation of N40, or 2.88 per cent. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official window, the naira also weakened to N1,363.23 per dollar. Data from the NFEM showed that the currency depreciated by N7.43, or 0.55 per cent, from the N1,355.80 per dollar recorded on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s foreign exchange reserves stood at $43.64 billion as of November 14, compared with $45.56 billion recorded on January 2. The figures, obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), indicated a decline of $1.92 billion, or 4.21 per cent, in the country’s external reserves since the beginning of the year. In a related development, the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) on Wednesday signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, energy financing and macroeconomic stability. The post Naira weakens to N1,470/$ at parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .
